title: Nottingham Forest’s Nicolo Savona set for knee surgery, may not play again this season
content:
Nottingham Forest’s Nicolo Savona is facing a fight to play again this season, with the defender set to undergo surgery on a knee injury on Tuesday.

The 22-year-old Italian has been sidelined since mid-January with the problem, last featuring for Forest in the 1-0 Europa League defeat in Braga.

Forest had hoped the injury, which he suffered in training, would resolve itself with rest. But the issue has not improved.

“I think tomorrow (Tuesday) is the surgery. He needs to have surgery,” said head coach Vitor Pereira in his Monday press conference ahead of Wednesday’s trip to face Manchester City.

“I really don’t know (if he’ll play again this season). After the surgery, they will say something and will inform us, but it is difficult.”

Savona has made 20 appearances in all competitions for Forest, including 15 starts, since joining from Juventus in an £11.2million move in August. He has scored two Premier League goals.

Pereira expects goalkeeper Matz Sels to be ready to face City in Manchester.

The Belgium international returned earlier than had been suspected from a groin injury to play against Brighton, but did need on-pitch treatment to get through the game.

Sels was pushed into action because of a calf injury sustained by Stefan Ortega against Fenerbahce last week.

“He needs to work to recover his power in his leg. But he feels okay. I hope that he will be ready for the next game,” Pereira replied when asked if Sels would be ready to play. “Ortega, I think he will be out for a few more days.

“We had a conversation with Sels and tried to explain we needed him in this moment, even though he needed more days to be fit and be in shape. But he is a leader and a person with strong character. He wanted to help the team and he decided to accept the challenge.

“Between me, him and the medical department, we decided to take the risk to play.”
